trigger: the audit store fails to persist a policy.dispatch row (pool timeout or INSERT error) on a tick or post-fix-check refusal
summary: policy.dispatch row said 'a refusal that changed a status is never left without a row'. AuditStore::log is synchronous fail-hard and record_denial discards its result for tick and post-fix-check origins, so a row is lost when the audit store fails to persist it: an advertised audit-completeness control the code does not enforce (I6(a) false assurance). The reporter labelled it MEDIUM (race-scoped sentence plus the YuzuAuditPersistFailures alert); the derived band governs per SKILL.md and E6 is not established. Same root as the false 'fire-and-forget' comment (g01-gov-13). The sentence came from the owner's ruling text (record the race and its reasoning); the fix keeps the race content and adds the limit.
classification_rationale: doc claim contradicts code behaviour next to an audit control

trigger: repeated or parallel POST /api/policies/{id}/evaluate on a large refused policy
summary: A refused /evaluate creates no in_flight_ entry, so the dedupe does not apply: every call redoes resolve_targets and all chunk upserts, and mark_blocked holds ONE pool lease across all 500-row chunks (about 1-3 s at 100k targets, estimated; about 16 concurrent calls could saturate the default pool). Operator with Policy:Execute. Not HIGH: bounded degrade, not a wedge and not the serialised-security-path I5(b) case.
classification_rationale: missing dedupe and lease bound; reasoned, not measured

severity_native: MEDIUM (HIGH if the retry cap counts as a wedge, I5(c))
trigger: gated post-check pair; operator /remediate three times
summary: A post-fix check refused after the fix ran leaves fix_attempt_count incremented (cap 3); repeated operator remediations run the fix with no verification, then claim_remediation refuses permanently, and the message says retry cap rather than the refusal. Reachable via pack-installed policies or an instruction edited after authoring. ADJUDICATION FOR THE OWNER: I did not apply I5(c). The cap is the pre-existing designed bound (kMaxFixAttempts=3), any fix that never verifies compliant burns attempts the same way, and exits exist (a compliant verdict; invalidate_policy resets fix_attempt_count, policy_store.cpp:1598 and 1623). Recorded at the derived MEDIUM; please confirm.
classification_rationale: hidden cause, not a wrong result; I3 not recorded because the retry-cap message is itself true

classification_rationale: stored evidence overwritten; reasoned
